text.p: Headlines from major national newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
EL PAIS
- Britain's Prime Minister Major resorts to fear in a final attempt to avoid an almost certain Blair victory.
- State supreme Judge Urculo submits his resignations to the government, radio station SER reported.
- Spanish Prime Minister Aznar sells Spain as a solid and valuable assett.
- A car bomb placed by ETA forces the evacuation of 140 people in Renteria.
- Real Madrid coach Fabio Capello faces first insults after announcing he is quitting the club.
EL MUNDO
- The government recognises all rights, except adoption, for unmarried couples living together.
- Real Madrid will no sack Capello to avoid paying a compensation of 600 million pesetas
- Basque ETA causes panic placing a car bomb in Renteria
LA VANGUARDIA
- The attacks against the unions by IU's leader Anguita breaks his mayority.
- For the first time ever it will be possible to pay taxes with credit cards
CINCO DIAS
- Very sweet economy. Local markets hit new records, Wall Street yesterday rose 2.64%, and the labour deal boosts new jobs
- Seven out of ten taxpayers are giving money in advance to Inland Revenue.
- Law rules out that Mexican Televisa wholly controls Cadena Iberica.
EXPANSION
- Banks increase profits despite lower interest rates.
- Repsol shares traded for more than 46 billion, and bourse hit record high
GACETA DE LOS NEGOCIOS
- Stocks hit a new record high, backed by Repsol
- Santander's profit 23.7 pct higher to 24.8 billion pesetas in the first quarter.
- General Electric is considering investing more than 90 billion pesetas in Murcia (Indonesia and the Netherland competitor's areas)
- Prime Minister Aznar promotes Spanish investment in Wall Street
- Inland Revenue will have to return 230 billion pesetas to taxpayers from mid-June.
-- Madrid Newsroom, + 341 585 8340
